citation.title: Global Oil & Gas Exit List 2024: Definitions and Methodology
citation.type: NGO methodology document accompanying a public database (Excel)

question: Not framed as a research question. The document explains what each column of the GOGEL database means and which thresholds a company must meet to be listed.
data: GOGEL 2024 database: upstream data from Rystad Energy (production 2023, resources as of September 2024, exploration CAPEX 2022-2024 average); midstream and gas/oil-fired power project detection from Global Energy Monitor; revenue and power portfolio research from company reports; project research from government sources and news outlets. Number of companies is not stated in this document.
method: Companies are listed in three tabs (Upstream, Midstream Expansion, Oil and Gas-Fired Power Expansion). A company is included when it meets at least one stated threshold in that tab (production, unconventional production, short-term expansion, exploration CAPEX, pipeline length, LNG capacity, gas- or oil-fired power capacity). Revenue share, power portfolio and reputational-risk projects are researched from company sources and reported as further columns.

definitions.term: GOGEL (scope: companies operating in the oil and gas industry)
definitions.definition: A public database on companies operating in the oil and gas industry. No separate criterion for what makes a company an 'oil and gas company' is stated.
definitions.quote: GOGEL is an extensive public database that provides information on companies operating in the oil and gas industry.

definitions.definition: Upstream companies are included if they produced at least 20 mmboe of oil, gas, condensate and NGL in 2023.
definitions.quote: GOGEL includes all companies that produced ≥ 20 mmboe in 2023.

definitions.definition: Categories describing a company's activity along the oil and gas value chain, sorted by revenue where possible.
definitions.quote: This column includes oil and gas subcategories to specify the business activities carried out by a company along the oil and gas value chain.
O&G E&P: All upstream activities (exploration, development and production of oil and gas)
O&G Midstream: Transmission, transportation and storage of oil and gas

definitions.term: Rystad Upstream Industry Segment: Independent vs E&P company
definitions.definition: Segment split of upstream-oriented companies at 50 kboe/day production.
definitions.quote: Independent: Upstream-oriented companies with production exceeding 50 kboe/day

definitions.definition: Column F gives the official name of the company; column G gives either the legal name of the parent (blue cells) or a relevant upstream subsidiary (white cells). All data in the row refer to the entity in column G.
definitions.quote: This column either provides the legal name of the parent company (blue cells) or a relevant upstream subsidiary (white cells). All further data points in the row refer to the company listed in column G.

definitions.definition: Filter for majority owned upstream subsidiaries.
definitions.quote: This column allows users to filter for majority owned upstream subsidiaries.

definitions.definition: Includes parent companies and companies without a majority owner.
definitions.quote: This column includes parent companies and companies without a majority owner.

definitions.definition: Majority owned subsidiaries and special purpose vehicles are covered if directly involved in pipeline or LNG expansion and above thresholds.
definitions.quote: GOGEL aims to continuously improve coverage of relevant subsidiaries and special purpose vehicles (SPVs) if they are directly involved in Pipeline or LNG expansion projects and above GOGEL thresholds.

definitions.definition: Same approach for gas-fired power expansion projects.
definitions.quote: GOGEL aims to continuously improve coverage of relevant subsidiaries and special purpose vehicles (SPVs) if they are directly involved in gas-fired power expansion projects and above GOGEL thresholds.

definitions.definition: Share of total operational revenue from fossil fuel related activities across the value chain, including coal. It is a reported metric, not a listing criterion.
definitions.quote: All business activities related to the fossil fuel value chain are included in this assessment (upstream, midstream, downstream, power).

proxies.indicator: Hydrocarbons production in 2023 of at least 20 mmboe (Rystad Energy data)
proxies.quote: This column indicates if a company meets our production threshold (≥ 20 mmboe).

proxies.indicator: Production of at least 2 mmboe from unconventional sources in 2023
proxies.quote: This column indicates if a company meets our unconventional production threshold (≥ 2 mmboe).

proxies.indicator: Intent to add at least 20 mmboe of resources under development or field evaluation
proxies.quote: GOGEL covers all companies that intend to add ≥ 20 mmboe of resources to their production portfolio in the near future.

proxies.indicator: Average exploration CAPEX 2022-2024 of at least USD 10 million
proxies.quote: GOGEL covers all companies with an average exploration CAPEX ≥ USD 10 million.

proxies.indicator: Responsible for at least 100 km of pipelines under development
proxies.quote: GOGEL covers all companies responsible for ≥ 100 km of pipelines under development.

proxies.indicator: At least 1 Mt of annual LNG terminal capacity under development
proxies.quote: GOGEL covers all companies responsible for ≥ 1 Mt of annual LNG terminal capacity under development.

proxies.indicator: At least 100 MW of gas-fired capacity under development
proxies.quote: GOGEL covers all companies responsible for ≥ 100 MW of GFP capacity under development.

proxies.indicator: At least 100 MW of oil-fired capacity under development
proxies.quote: GOGEL covers all companies responsible for ≥ 100 MW of OFP capacity under development.

proxies.indicator: IEA NZE Expansion Overshoot above 0 and/or Exploration CAPEX above 0
proxies.quote: A company is marked if it has an IEA NZE Expansion Overshoot (column Y) above 0 and/or Exploration CAPEX (column Z) above 0.

proxies.indicator: Subsidiary flagged in the Type of Subsidiary column; the percentage that counts as majority is not stated
proxies.quote: This column allows users to filter for majority owned subsidiaries.

findings.claim: The upstream part of the list is stated to cover over 90% of global production, planned short-term expansion and exploration expenditure (authors' claim, no calculation shown).
findings.quote: The companies listed in the upstream part of GOGEL account for over 90% of annual global hydrocarbons production, over 90% of planned short-term upstream expansion, and over 90% of exploration expenditures.

findings.claim: All exploration spending is treated as incompatible with the IEA NZE scenario (authors' position).
findings.quote: Thus, all expenditure displayed in this column constitutes an overshoot of the NZE scenario

limitations.point: The IEA NZE benchmark rests on optimistic assumptions and is a minimum standard.
limitations.quote: However, the scenario is partially based on very optimistic assumptions.

limitations.point: Coverage is incomplete and will be extended to further subsectors.
limitations.quote: GOGEL will be updated each fall and amended over time by including further subsectors of the oil & gas industry and by increasing coverage.

limitations.point: Revenue share data are sometimes unavailable, estimated or lower bounds.
limitations.quote: insufficient reporting: The company does not adequately differentiate between fossil fuel related and fossil fuel unrelated business activities

limitations.point: The document does not define a trade association, an enterprise or a general 'oil and gas company', and states no revenue-share or ownership-percentage threshold for inclusion. Absence only; the document is silent, not negative.
The document is an advocacy organisation's methodology note, not independent research. Authors field of metadata lists only 'Fiona'. No instructions to readers or AI were found in the text.
